subject: reasoning
question: A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. Only two people sit between D and A when counted from the left of A. C sits third to the left of G. E sits to the immediate right of G. E sits second to the left of D. F is an immediate neighbour of C. How many people sit between B and G when counted from the left of G?
solution:
**Given: **A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table facing the centre.

1. C sits third to the left of G.

2. E sits to the immediate right of G.

3. E sits second to the left of D.

4. F is an immediate neighbour of C.

5. Only two people sit between D and A when counted from the left of A.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3574f4ad54f8adc0345567eb6a91c9698dfccedc7553b5d59264f5d95f5226f9.png] 

B, the only person left will occupy the vacant position.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/593f0cbe83d205a31d72c5198e48d7fd2abbad3ddd95fd9a074d29edd3683155.png] 

Thus, four people sit between B and G when counted from the left of G.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 3".
